## Analysis
The search has converged on a robust dense-core/fringe basin: many unrelated local, genetic, Pareto, and destroy–repair methods reproduce \(n=66\), but none improve it. Larger tensor and affine-copy constructions raise scores only to 1.084, while unrestricted coordinate searches fail, showing that structure—not search intensity—is decisive. Copy-union experiments capped at seven layers missed the smallest classical eight-point MSTD multiplier; its product with the 66-point incumbent has 528 points, only 16 above the limit. This creates a new boundary regime where carry-free product structure can be retained while optimizing a small deletion set.
